question:

question:
In the given figure, a square ABCD is inscribed in a quadrant APCQ. If AB = 16 cm. Find the area of the shaded region (take π = 3.14 ) correct to two places of decimal.

(CGL 2022 Pre)
options:
155.98 cm2

179.68 cm2

163.85 cm2

145.92 cm2
solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e. 145.92 cm2.

The radius of the quadrant of the circle = the diagonal of the square

In square ABCD,

AC = \(16\sqrt2\) cm

Area of shaded region = Area of quadrant - Area of square

⇒ \(\frac{1}{4} \pi r^2 - 16^2\) 

⇒ \(\frac{1}{4} ×3.14× 512 - 256\)

⇒ 3.14 × 128 − 256

⇒ 128(3.14 − 2)

⇒ 128 × 1.14 = 145.92 cm2
question_hi:
दी गई आकृति में, एक वर्ग ABCD एक चतुर्थांश APCQ में अंकित है। यदि AB = 16 सेमी है। छायांकित क्षेत्र का क्षेत्रफल ज्ञात करें (π = 3.14 लें) दशमलव के दो स्थानों तक सही।

(CGL 2022 Pre)
options_hi:
155.98 सेमी2

179.68 सेमी2

163.85 सेमी2

145.92 सेमी2
solution_hi:
सही उत्तर विकल्प 4 अर्थात 145.92 सेमी2 है।

वृत्त के चतुर्थांश की त्रिज्या = वर्ग का विकर्ण

वर्ग ABCD में,

AC = \(16\sqrt2\) सेमी

छायांकित क्षेत्र का क्षेत्रफल = चतुर्थांश का क्षेत्रफल - वर्ग का क्षेत्रफल

⇒ \(\frac{1}{4} \pi r^2 - 16^2\) 

⇒ \(\frac{1}{4} ×3.14× 512 - 256\)

⇒ 3.14 × 128 − 256

⇒ 128(3.14 − 2)

⇒ 128 × 1.14 = 145.92 सेमी2

question:
What is the perimeter of a square inscribed in a circle of radius 5 cm?

(CGL MAINS 2022)
solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. 20 \(\sqrt2 \) cm.

Diagonal = a\(\sqrt2\) = 10 cm

A = side of square = \(d \over \sqrt2\) = \(10 \over \sqrt2\)

⇒ \({10 \over \sqrt2}\times{\sqrt2\over \sqrt2}\) = \(5\sqrt2\)

A = वर्ग की भुजा = \(d \over \sqrt2\) = \(10 \over \sqrt2\)

⇒ \({10 \over \sqrt2}\times{\sqrt2\over \sqrt2}\) = \(5\sqrt2\)

परिमाप = 4 × \(5\sqrt2\) = 20\(\sqrt2\) सेमी

question:

△ABE में

question:
In the given figure, AB = DB & AC = DC. If ∠ABD = 58° and ∠DBC = (2x − 4)°, ∠ACB = (y + 15)° and ∠DCB = 63°, then the value of 2x + 5y is:

(CGL 2022 Pre)
solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. 273°.

AB = DB, AC = DC, and BC is common.

∴ △ABC ≅ △DBC

∴ ∠ABC = △DBC = \(∠ABD\over2\)

⇒ ∠ABC = \(58\over2​\) = 29°

So, (2x − 4) = 29°

⇒ 2x = 33°

Now, ∠ACB = ∠DCB = 63°

∴ (y + 15) = 63°

∴ y = 48°

⇒ 2x + 5y = 33 + 5 × 48 = 33 + 240 = 273
question_hi:

(CGL 2022 Pre)
solution_hi:
सही उत्तर विकल्प 2 अर्थात 273° है।

AB = DB, AC = DC, तथा BC उभयनिष्ठ है।

∴ △ABC ≅ △DBC

∴ ∠ABC = △DBC = \(∠ABD\over2\)

⇒ ∠ABC = \(58\over2​\) = 29°

इसलिए, (2x − 4) = 29°

⇒ 2x = 33°

अब, ∠ACB = ∠DCB = 63°

∴ (y + 15) = 63°

∴ y = 48°

⇒ 2x + 5y = 33 + 5 × 48 = 33 + 240 = 273

question:
WXYZ is a quadrilateral in which XQ and ZP are perpendicular to WY such that XQ = ZP. Diagonals ZX and WY intersect each other at point O. If OX = 12 cm, then find the value of ZX (in cm).

(SSC CGL PRE 2024)
solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e 24.

ZP = XQ (given)

∠ZOP = ∠XOQ (Vertically opposite angles)

and, ∠ZPO = ∠XQO = 90∘

∴ △ZOP ∼ △XQO

⇒ \(\frac{ZP}{XQ} = \frac{OZ}{OX}\)

⇒ \({1 \over 1 }= \frac{OZ}{12}\)

∴ OZ = 12 cm

⇒​​​​​​​ ZX = 12 + 12 = 24 cm
question_hi:
WXYZ एक चतुर्भुज है जिसमें XQ और ZP, WY पर इस प्रकार लंबवत हैं कि XQ = ZP है। विकर्ण ZX और WY एक दूसरे को बिंदु O पर प्रतिच्छेद करते हैं। यदि OX = 12 सेमी है, तो ZX का मान (सेमी में) ज्ञात कीजिए।

(SSC CGL PRE 2024)
solution_hi:
सही उत्तर विकल्प 2 अर्थात 24 है।

​ZP = XQ (दिया गया है)

∠ZOP = ∠XOQ (ऊर्ध्वाधर विपरीत कोण)

और, ∠ZPO = ∠XQO = 90∘

∴ △ZOP ∼ △XQO

⇒ \(\frac{ZP}{XQ} = \frac{OZ}{OX}\)

⇒ \({1 \over 1 }= \frac{OZ}{12}\)

∴ OZ = 12 सेमी

⇒ ZX = 12 + 12 = 24 सेमी

question:
Two equilateral triangles of side \(10\sqrt3\) ​ cm are joined to form a quadrilateral. What is the altitude of the quadrilateral?

(CPO 2019 Pre)
solution:

question:
M is the midpoint of the side QR of a parallelogram. PQRS (P being on the top left hand, followed by other points going clockwise). The line SM is drawn intersecting PQ produced at T. What is the length (in terms of the length of SR) of PT?

(CHSL 2023 Pre)
solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e 2SR.

PT is parallel to SR

In a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal

∴ SR = PQ

Therefore, SR = PQ = QT

∴ PT = 2SR

solution_hi:

∠QMT = ∠SMR (उर्ध्वाधरतः विपरीत कोण )

∴ △SMR ∼ △TMQ

\(\frac{SR}{QT} = \frac{MR}{MQ} = \frac{SM}{MT} = \frac{1}{1}\)

∴ SR = QT

समांतर चतुर्भुज में सम्मुख भुजाएँ बराबर होती हैं

∴ SR = PQ

इसलिए, SR = PQ = QT

∴ PT = 2SR

question:
In a parallelogram ABCD, if vertices are in respective order and diagonals AC and BD intersect at O, then which of the following is NOT always correct?

SP 2023 Phase-11 Matric. L
solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e. ΔAOD ≅  ΔCOD.

In the parallelogram, opposite triangles made by the diagonals are always congruent.

∴ △AOB ≅ △COD and △AOD ≅ △BOC

In the parallelogram, one diagonal converts the parallelogram into two congruent triangles

∴ △ABC ≅ △ADC

Since AD = CD

∴ Hence △AOD is not congruent to △COD.

SP 2023 Phase-11 Matric. L

समांतर चतुर्भुज में विकर्णों द्वारा बनाए गए सम्मुख त्रिभुज सदैव सर्वांगसम होते हैं।

∴ △AOB ≅ △COD और △AOD ≅ △BOC

समांतर चतुर्भुज में, एक विकर्ण समांतर चतुर्भुज को दो समतुल्य त्रिभुजों में परिवर्तित करता है।

∴ △ABC ≅ △ADC

अतः AD = CD

∴ अतः △AOD, △COD के समतुल्य नहीं है।

ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. The tangents to the circle at the points A and C on it, intersect at P. If ∠ABC = 58o, then what is the measure of ∠APC?

(CPO 2019 Pre)
solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e. 64°.

∠AOC = 2 × ∠ABC = 2 × 58° = 116°

∠APC = 180° − ∠AOC = 180° – 116° = 64°

question:
OABC is a quadrilateral. where O is the center of a circle and A, B, and C are points on the circle, such that ∠ABC = 120o. What is the ratio of the measure of ∠AOC to that of ∠OAC?

(CHSL 2018 Pre)
solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. 4 : 1.

\(\frac{\angle AOC}{\angle OAC} = \frac{\alpha}{\beta}\)

⇒ ∠ADC = 180 − ∠ABC

⇒ ∠ADC = 180° – 120° = 60° (Sum of opposite angle in quadrilateral is 180o)

⇒ ∠AOC = 2 × 60° = 120° (minor arc) [The Angle formed at the center is double of the angle formed at the circumference]

⇒ OC = OA = radius

⇒ ∠OAC = ∠OCA

In △OAC

⇒ ∠OAC + ∠ACO + ∠COA = 180°

⇒ 2∠OAC + 120° = 180°

⇒ ∠OAC = \(\frac{180° - 120° }{2} = \frac{60° }{2} = 30° \)

Ratio → α : β

⇒ 120° : 30° = 4 : 1
